summary: Digest-bound independent semantic review of Lumen EC source sha256:f297767e0ed16d63869024d4bcf5d5fdcbd57d1ce636b1c4e82f974c4dfdd860. The revised stability contracts close the prior false-green defects: Rig now drives real toxiproxy packet-loss and partition phases with baseline/fault/recovery measurements; endurance scenarios resolve the unique live Lumen listener and independently sample RSS, FD, socket, and thread counts around bounded-keyspace work; the overload case declares a real 600-QPS, 16-worker, 30-second open-loop workload with measured error-rate/p99 pins and a 95% achieved-QPS honesty gate; and latency drift is measured across three non-empty 500-search windows. The authored assertions pin concrete sample counts, failure constraints, recovery budgets, and numerical thresholds. Their oracles are outside Lumen (Rig scheduling/assertion evaluation, toxiproxy, ps/proc/lsof helpers, and retained benchmark baselines), and explicit positive-baseline, nonzero-fault, zero-failure, resource-bound, pin-presence, and load-honesty checks prevent empty or zero-sample success. The currently RED 600-QPS execution is not treated as passing runtime evidence: it remains a shared Rig HTTP transport/harness blocker to resolve before EC verification can pass, while the EC contract itself is specific, non-vacuous, and independently verifiable. All six semantic axes pass; findings are empty.
